result.title: Failure Recovery via Belief Updates and World Modeling for Long-Horizon Agents
result.summary: Long-horizon agents often struggle to recover from failures whose causes lie several steps earlier, beyond what local reflection or backtracking can resolve. We introduce BELIEFWEAVER, a framework that combines persistent evidence across attempts with prospective reasoning over repair directions. It maintains a relational belief state over frontiers, attempts, observations, and checkpoints. Execution evidence updates related frontier priorities across attempts and rollback, while diagnostic evidence gates execution. An implicit world model (IWM) evaluates repair hypotheses, predicts progress, and identifies relations among frontiers to guide exploration. We further distill these recurring IWM reasoning components into a 9B student through supervised fine-tuning and on-policy distillation (OPD). Across three terminal-based benchmarks, BELIEFWEAVER improves aggregate final score by 5.1 percentage points over native Terminus-2 continuation, with positive trends in exploration efficiency. The distilled 9B student improves final score by 9.8 percentage points over the reported native baseline while reducing estimated teacher API cost by 54.8% relative to the matched teacher. These results show that persistent evidence and prospective reasoning can improve recovery in long-horizon agent tasks while substantially reducing reliance on teacher-model inference.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 BELIEFWEAVER，在长程 terminal 智能体中维护跨尝试与回滚的关系型 belief state，用执行与诊断证据更新 frontier 优先级，并以隐式 world model 评估修复假设、预测进展，再将其推理组件蒸馏到 9B 学生模型，在三个基准上提升最终分数并降低教师调用成本。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本 agent 的 belief 更新、证据门控与前瞻假设评估，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态维护、证据筛选及停止／修复决策的借鉴线索，但原文不涉及视觉或多模态推理，迁移属推测。
